# clastIndexOfRow

> Return the index of the last row in a single-precision complex floating-point input matrix which has the same elements as a provided search vector.

<section class="intro">

</section>

<!-- /.intro -->

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```javascript
var clastIndexOfRow = require( '@stdlib/blas/ext/base/ndarray/clast-index-of-row' );
```

#### clastIndexOfRow( arrays )

Returns the index of the last row in a single-precision complex floating-point input matrix which has the same elements as a provided search vector.

<!-- eslint-disable max-len -->

```javascript
var Complex64Matrix = require( '@stdlib/ndarray/matrix/complex64' );
var Complex64Vector = require( '@stdlib/ndarray/vector/complex64' );
var Uint8Array = require( '@stdlib/array/uint8' );
var ndarray = require( '@stdlib/ndarray/ctor' );
var clastIndexOfRow = require( '@stdlib/blas/ext/base/ndarray/clast-index-of-row' );

var A = new Complex64Matrix( [ [ 1.0, 0.0, 2.0, 0.0 ], [ 3.0, 0.0, 4.0, 0.0 ], [ 3.0, 0.0, 4.0, 0.0 ] ] );
var x = new Complex64Vector( [ 3.0, 0.0, 4.0, 0.0 ] );
var workspace = new ndarray( 'uint8', new Uint8Array( 3 ), [ 3 ], [ 1 ], 0, 'row-major' );

var out = clastIndexOfRow( [ A, x, workspace ] );
// returns 2
```

The function has the following parameters:

-   **arrays**: array-like object containing the following ndarrays:

    -   a two-dimensional input ndarray corresponding to `A`.
    -   a one-dimensional input ndarray corresponding to `x`.
    -   a one-dimensional workspace ndarray.

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   If the function is provided an empty matrix or if the function is unable to find a matching row, the function returns `-1` (i.e., an invalid index).
-   The `workspace` array is only applicable when an input matrix is stored in column-major order. When the matrix is stored in row-major order, the workspace array is ignored.
-   When searching for a matching row, the function checks for equality using the strict equality operator `===`. As a consequence, `NaN` values are considered distinct, and `-0` and `+0` are considered the same.

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

<!-- eslint no-undef: "error" -->

<!-- eslint-disable max-len -->

```javascript
var discreteUniform = require( '@stdlib/random/array/discrete-uniform' );
var Complex64Matrix = require( '@stdlib/ndarray/matrix/complex64' );
var Complex64Vector = require( '@stdlib/ndarray/vector/complex64' );
var Uint8Array = require( '@stdlib/array/uint8' );
var ndarray2array = require( '@stdlib/ndarray/to-array' );
var ndarray = require( '@stdlib/ndarray/ctor' );
var clastIndexOfRow = require( '@stdlib/blas/ext/base/ndarray/clast-index-of-row' );

var opts = {
    'dtype': 'float32'
};

var A = new Complex64Matrix( discreteUniform( 5*5*2, -50, 50, opts ).buffer, 0, 5, 5 );
console.log( ndarray2array( A ) );

var x = new Complex64Vector( discreteUniform( 5*2, -50, 50, opts ).buffer, 0, 5 );
console.log( ndarray2array( x ) );

var workspace = new ndarray( 'uint8', new Uint8Array( 5 ), [ 5 ], [ 1 ], 0, 'row-major' );

var out = clastIndexOfRow( [ A, x, workspace ] );
console.log( out );
```

</section>
